questions.question: In process synchronization, what does the Wait (P) operation do to a semaphore?

options.C: Resets its value back to one
options.D: Sets its value permanently to zero

questions.explanation: Wait (P) decrements the semaphore value and acts as a block system call. Signal (V) increments it and acts as a wakeup call.

questions.concept: Invalid input combination of S-R flip-flop
questions.question: Which input combination is invalid for an S-R flip-flop?
questions.explanation: In an S-R flip-flop, the input S = 1, R = 1 is invalid. The other combinations hold, reset or set the stored bit.

questions.concept: Licklider introduced cloud concepts in the 1960s
questions.question: Who introduced the concepts of cloud computing in the 1960s?
questions.explanation: Joseph Carl Robnett (J.C.R.) Licklider introduced cloud concepts in the 1960s. Cloud computing means storing and accessing data and programs over the Internet.

questions.question: Which SQL command removes all rows of a table without a WHERE clause while keeping the table structure?
questions.explanation: TRUNCATE deletes all rows faster and does not use a WHERE clause, but keeps the table structure. DELETE removes selected rows with WHERE, and DROP removes the whole table.

questions.question: In C++, which symbol returns the memory address of a variable?
questions.explanation: The & symbol returns the memory address of a variable. The * symbol declares pointers and acts as the dereference operator, and new allocates memory dynamically.

questions.concept: Register machine equivalence to Turing machine
questions.question: Which of the following models is considered equivalent in computational power to a Turing machine?
questions.explanation: Register machines, multi-tape and multi-track Turing machines are listed as equivalent models of the Turing machine. Finite automata, PDA and LBA are less powerful.

questions.concept: Key logger is a type of spyware
questions.question: A key logger, which secretly records the keys pressed by a user, is a type of:
questions.explanation: A key logger is a type of spyware. Ransomware restricts access and demands ransom, while a worm self-replicates across a network.

questions.question:
What happens when this Python code runs?
s = 'Hello'
print(s[10])
questions.explanation: Accessing a string index outside the valid range raises IndexError. A non-integer index would raise TypeError instead.

questions.question: A streaming service lets users play, pause and fast forward a movie. Which protocol controls such media sessions between client and server?
questions.explanation: RTSP (Real-Time Streaming Protocol) controls media sessions, as in Netflix play/pause/fast forward. RTP is used for video conferencing and live streaming.

questions.question: Using the laws of Boolean algebra, the expression A + A'·B simplifies to:
questions.explanation: By the absorption law, A + A'·B = A + B. The related form A + A·B simplifies to A.

questions.question: Which term refers to the measure of functional strength of a single software module?
questions.explanation: Cohesion measures the functional strength of a module, while coupling measures interdependence between modules. Good design has strong cohesion and low coupling.

questions.question: Which of the following are examples of simplex (one-way only) communication? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Simplex allows one-way communication only; examples include TV broadcasting and fire alarm systems. A walkie-talkie is half duplex and video conferencing is full duplex.

questions.question: What is the time complexity of Dijkstra's shortest path algorithm, where V is the number of vertices and E the number of edges?
questions.explanation: Dijkstra's algorithm runs in O(E log V). Floyd-Warshall takes O(V^3) and Bellman-Ford takes O(V x E).

questions.concept: Number of frames from physical address bits
questions.question: A system has a 27-bit logical address, a 21-bit physical address and a page size of 1K. How many frames does physical memory have?
questions.explanation: Page size 1K = 2^10, so offset d = 10 bits. Frame bits F = 21 - 10 = 11, giving 2^11 = 2048 frames (the 131072 figure is the number of pages, 2^17).

questions.concept: Logic bomb triggered by time is a time bomb
questions.question: When a logic bomb is activated by a time-related event, it is known as a:
questions.explanation: A logic bomb that is activated by a time-related event is called a time bomb. A retrovirus is a virus that can delete anti-virus software.

questions.question: Which LPWAN technology is a French global network operator offering an inexpensive, reliable, low-power solution to connect sensors and devices?
questions.explanation: Sigfox is a French global network operator providing a low-power solution for connecting sensors and devices. LoRaWAN, NB-IoT (Cat-M2) and Cat-1 are other LPWAN technologies.

questions.question: Which Python keyword is used for returning values from a generator?
questions.explanation: yield returns values from a generator. return exits a function and returns a value, lambda creates an anonymous function, and pass executes nothing.

questions.concept: Minimum Hamming distance between valid Hamming codewords
questions.question: In Hamming codes such as the common Hamming(7, 4), what is the minimal Hamming distance between any two correct codewords?
questions.explanation: The minimal Hamming distance between any two correct Hamming codewords is 3, which allows single-bit error correction. Hamming codes were invented by Richard Hamming.

questions.concept: Actions in a single Turing machine move
questions.question: In one move, what can a Turing machine do?

options.A: Push or pop a symbol on a stack only
options.B: Read a symbol but never write anything on the tape
options.C: Jump the head to any cell of the tape
options.D: Change state, write a symbol, move head one cell

questions.explanation: In one move a Turing machine may change state, write a symbol, and move its head left or right by one cell. Stack operations belong to pushdown automata.

questions.question: The SAVEPOINT command belongs to which category of SQL language?
questions.explanation: TCL (Transaction Control Language) includes COMMIT, ROLLBACK and SAVEPOINT. DCL has GRANT and REVOKE.

questions.question: Which networking standard is defined by IEEE 802.4?
questions.explanation: IEEE 802.4 is Token Bus. Token Ring is 802.5, Logical Link Control is 802.2 and Cable Modems is 802.14.

questions.question: Transforming a pixel-based (raster) image into a vector image is called:
questions.explanation: Vectorization converts a raster image into a vector image; rasterization is the reverse. Morphing and warping are image animation/distortion techniques.

questions.question: As per operator precedence rules used for expression conversion, which operator group is evaluated from right to left?
questions.explanation: Exponentiation (^) has right-to-left associativity. Parentheses, multiplication/division and addition/subtraction are evaluated left to right.

questions.question: A team adds new features to an existing, working software product. This type of maintenance is called:
questions.explanation: Perfective maintenance adds new features to existing software. Adaptive maintenance updates software to fit new environments.

questions.concept: Founder of OOPS is Alan Kay
questions.question: Who is regarded as the founder of Object-Oriented Programming (OOPS) in the 1960s?
questions.explanation: Alan Kay is credited as the founder of OOPS in the 1960s. Simula (1967) was the first OOP language and Smalltalk the first pure object-oriented language.
